caveats: Cold paint time overstates the app (CPU painter stands in for the WebGL painter); warm time is structural (a hit skips decode, paint and encode entirely).
Absolute seconds do not transfer to the T470; cold-vs-warm ratio and ms/frame are the signal.
"Segments" is the fx-segment count (one rendered clip segment per effect-bearing clip), not per-effect shader cost.

4K x 20 was not measured: the run was killed during that cell (OOM on this VM + the 2400 s shell timeout). Its cold cost extrapolates to ~1500 s at the 4K x 5 rate of 2.48 s/frame; the warm cost extrapolates to milliseconds (every other warm cell is < 60 ms total). The extrapolation is labelled, not measured.
host: shared dev VM (no GPU, shared vCPUs) — not the ThinkPad T470 reference laptop; absolute seconds do not transfer
method: FxJobs fx pass (decode + deterministic CPU paint + encode) per clip segment; 1 s segments at 30 fps; cold = first render into an empty cache, warm = new session over the same cache.
reading: The cache is the whole story: warm (cache-hit) renders are 3-4 orders of magnitude cheaper than cold renders at every measured cell (warm/cold 0.000-0.003). Cold cost scales with pixels (4K ~2.5-4x 1080p per frame) and with segment count (linear). On this VM a cold 4K frame costs ~1.6-2.5 s through the CPU stand-in painter — that absolute number is the painter's, not the app's; the ratio is what transfers.
